correctness.rationale: For three independent volume-uniform points of the unit d-ball and fixed d>=2, start with the published exact 3/kappa_d expected ball-segment volume identity. Uniformly for 0<=|s|<=ell<=1, the difference of square roots equals (ell²-s²)/(2R) * [1+(ell²+s²)/(4R²)+O(R^-4)]; integrate its (d-1)st power. Beta ratio I1/I0=2(d+1)ell²/(2d+1). From published half-distance moments, E L^(2d+1)/E L^(2d-1) = ((3d-1)/(3d+1))*3d/(4d+1), yielding a_d=3d(d²-1)(3d-1)/(2(2d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1)). Independently verified rational d2 through d12; d2=1/7 is prior-known and expressly non-novel, d3=144/455, C3=3/55, second tail coeff 432/25025. For maxima, k log(1-P) contains geometry k^-2/(d-1); at d3 binomial correction k^-1 also contributes 1/2, total 1147/182. Remainder uniformly integrable because ell<=1 and fixed d.

value.rationale: The coefficient explicitly resolves the first term concealed in a recent sharp all-dimensional O(R^-2)-relative remainder and quantitatively controls finite-sample convergence to the Fréchet extreme-value limit. For d>=4 the geometric correction dominates binomial error, whereas for d=3 both contribute. This is a natural quantitative refinement of the circumradius law, beyond recomputing the already-known planar coefficient.

limitations: Fixed dimension d>=2 and three volume-uniform points in unit Euclidean ball only.
